content.title: When is Eid ul-Fitr 2026 in India? March 20 or 21; when will the Moon be sighted; last fast of Ramadan and all you need to know
content.text: Eid ul-Fitr, the festival of breaking the fast, will be celebrated in India on March 20 or 21, 2026. The exact date depends on the crescent moon sighting. This joyous occasion marks the end of Ramadan. Families will reunite for prayers, feasts, and to exchange greetings. Children will receive Eidi gifts.Eid ul-Fitr is the biggest festival celebrated by Muslims across the globe, it marks the end of Ramadan, the holy month of dawn-to-dusk fasting, prayer, and quiet reflection.Families reunite, mosques fill with grateful voices, and the air buzzes with the scent of fresh sweets and savory feasts. In India, where diverse Muslim communities blend traditions, Eid brings neighbours together for "Eid Mubarak" greetings, shared plates of sheer khurma, and kids clutching Eidi envelopes.Amid bustling markets on Chand Raat, it's a reminder of renewal, charity, and unbreakable bonds. But with moon sighting being the deciding factor for the big day, people are eagerly waiting to know if Eid will be a Friday feast or a Saturday celebration.When is Eid ul-Fitr 2026 in India? Muslims break their fast on the first day of Shawwal, marked by the crescent moon sighting. Known as the "Festival of Breaking the Fast," it honors self-discipline, prayer, and compassion, reminding everyone to spread kindness after reflection.PollWhen do you think Eid ul-Fitr 2026 will be celebrated in India?Friday, March 20Saturday, March 21When will Eid ul-Fitr 2026 be celebrated in India?Eid ul-Fitr 2026 in India will likely fall on March 20 or 21, depending on the crescent moon sighting that signals the start of Shawwal. This "Festival of breaking the fast" ends Ramadan, with the exact date confirmed only after local committees spot the crescent moon in the skies on Chand Raat. As per the Islamic calendar, the month is either 29 or 30 days long, so spotting the chand will be the deciding factor. Why does the date for Eid shift every year?The Islamic lunar calendar tracks moon phases, making months 29 or 30 days long, about 10-11 days shorter than the solar year. So Eid moves earlier annually in the Gregorian calendar. In 2026, moonwatching happens on the evening of March 19 or 20. If sighted, Eid will fall on Friday, March 20. No sighting means 30-day Ramadan, pushing celebrations to Saturday, March 21. Astronomical data favors March 20 visibility across India, but local Ruet-e-Hilal Committees in Delhi, Lucknow, Hyderabad, and Mumbai make the call post-Maghrib namaaz. It's a gazetted holiday, often tentative till official word.Representative ImageChand raat is a festive buzzChand Raat thrills with late-night markets for new outfits, mehendi, sweets, and feast prep. Families spend time together shopping and anticipating, turning the eve into pure excitement. Day one begins with baths, best clothes, Zakat al-Fitr charity, and Salat al-Eid prayers at mosques or Eidgahs. "Eid Mubarak!" echoes as folks visit loved ones, swapping dishes like biryani and sewai. Known as "Sweet Eid," it spans 3 days of gifts (eidi for kids), feasts, and reflection, honoring Ramadan's spiritual growth.
